1.name: DCD
1.hint: data carrier detect input, active low; may stay open (Table 9)

2.name: RI
2.hint: ring indicator input, active low; may stay open (Table 9)

4.name: D+
4.hint: USB D+: integrated transceiver with on-chip matching and pull-up resistors – no external resistors (p. 1, section 6); TVS diodes at the connector recommended for ESD (Figure 5, option 3)

5.name: D-
5.hint: USB D−: integrated transceiver with on-chip matching and pull-up resistors – no external resistors (p. 1, section 6); TVS diodes at the connector recommended for ESD (Figure 5, option 3)

6.name: VDD
6.hint: 3.3 V regulator output (≤ 100 mA) in configurations 1 and 2; in configuration 3 (regulator bypassed) a 3.0–3.6 V supply input with REGIN tied to it – this entry describes configurations 1 and 2 (section 10)

needs.source: Silicon Labs CP2102/9 Single-Chip USB to UART Bridge data sheet, Rev. 1.7 (7/16), Figure 5 and Figures 6–7 (C4 0.1 µF at VDD; C3 4.7 µF added when the regulator powers other devices, option 2) – 0.1 µF read as the minimum: assumption

7.name: REGIN
7.hint: 5 V input of the on-chip regulator (Table 6: 4.0–5.25 V); in configuration 3 tied to the 3 V net

needs.source: Silicon Labs CP2102/9 Single-Chip USB to UART Bridge data sheet, Rev. 1.7 (7/16), section 10 note ('additional decoupling capacitance (e.g., 0.1 µF in parallel with 1.0 µF) to the REGIN input') and Figures 5–7 (1.0 µF + 0.1 µF) – read as at least 1 µF: assumption

8.name: VBUS
8.hint: VBUS sense input: connect to the USB VBUS; 5 V here means a USB connection (Table 9); detection threshold 1.0–2.9 V (Table 6)

9.name: RST#
9.hint: device reset: open-drain output of the internal POR / VDD monitor; driving it low for ≥ 15 µs resets (Table 9, Table 5); a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to VDD can be added for noise immunity (Figure 5, option 1)

10.name: NC
10.hint: leave unconnected or tie to VDD (Table 9)

11.name: SUSPEND#
11.hint: driven low in USB suspend (Table 9); floats high for a moment during reset (section 6)

12.name: SUSPEND
12.hint: driven high in USB suspend and until enumeration completes; floats high during reset – a 10 kΩ pull-down holds it low (section 6, Figure 5 option 4)

hints: Silicon Labs: for newer designs the CP2102N is recommended instead of the CP2102 (p. 1)

three supply configurations (section 10, Figures 6–10): 1 USB bus-powered and 2 self-powered with the regulator – REGIN 4.0–5.25 V, VDD the 3.3 V output; 3 regulator bypassed – 3.0–3.6 V into VDD, REGIN tied to it. The entry models 1 and 2 (behaviour ldo, VDD power_output); for configuration 3 the project's copy needs behaviour none and VDD as power_in
the regulator's output VDD powers external 3 V devices up to 100 mA in total (Table 6 note); with other devices on it add 4.7 µF at VDD (Figure 5, option 2)
UART I/O, VBUS and RST take up to 5.8 V (Table 2); VIH ≥ 2.0 V, VIL ≤ 0.8 V on the UART and suspend pins (Table 4); outputs swing to VDD (3.3 V)
a self-powered design whose VDD or REGIN can be unpowered while VBUS has 5 V needs a divider on VBUS to respect its absolute maximum (section 10)
sources: Silicon Labs CP2102/9 Single-Chip USB to UART Bridge data sheet, Rev. 1.7 (7/16), LCSC's copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/995f8cf35f204a56bfc0167d47351f08.pdf?productCode=C6568, read 2026-10-31 (silabs.com refused the download, HTTP 403)
pin definitions, Table 9, p. 10; QFN-28 pinout top view, Figure 2, p. 11 (centre pad labelled GND)

absolute maximum ratings, Table 2, p. 5: VDD −0.3 … 4.2 V; any I/O pin, VBUS or RST −0.3 … 5.8 V (CP2102); 500 mA total through VDD and GND; 100 mA sunk by RST or any I/O pin; ambient under bias −55 … 125 °C

recommended operating conditions, Table 3, p. 6: VDD 3.0 / 3.3 / 3.6 V; IPU 200 / 230 µA (USB pull-up); TA −40 … +85 °C; θJA 32 °C/W (multi-layer PCB, exposed pad soldered); CP2102 IREGIN 20 mA typ. / 26 mA max. normal, 80 / 100 µA suspended (note 3: add the pull-up current)
iq_a 0.02623 = IREGIN max. 26 mA + IPU max. 0.23 mA (Table 3, note 3)
UART and suspend I/O, Table 4, p. 7: CP2102 VIH ≥ 2.0 V, VIL ≤ 0.8 V; VOH ≥ VDD − 0.7 V at −3 mA, VOL ≤ 0.6 V at 8.5 mA; baud rate ≤ 921600 bps
reset, Table 5, p. 7: RST low ≥ 15 µs; CP2102 VIHRESET ≥ 0.7 × VDD, VILRESET ≤ 0.25 × VDD
regulator, Table 6, p. 8: CP2102 VREGIN 4.0–5.25 V; VDDOUT 3.0 / 3.3 / 3.6 V at 1–100 mA; VBUS detection threshold 1.0 / 1.8 / 2.9 V; maximum regulator supply current 100 mA (i_out_max_a)
USB transceiver, Table 7, p. 8: pull-up 1.425–1.575 kΩ, output impedance 38 Ω
typical connection, Figure 5, p. 14; regulator configurations and the REGIN decoupling note, section 10, p. 18–20; SUSPEND behaviour at reset, section 6, p. 14

behaviour ldo (REGIN role vin, VDD role vout, vout_v 3.3 typ.): the regulator of configurations 1 and 2 – the data sheet gives no dropout voltage, so the simulation's default applies below VREGIN 4.0 V, where vin_min_v switches the model off anyway: assumption
RoHS: p. 1 ('RoHS-compliant 28-pin QFN'), Table 1; LCSC product data C6568 (RoHS), 2026-10-31
mpn, manufacturer, footprint, jlc_class, pin numbers and names: EasyEDA library data of C6568 via edakit part import, read 2026-10-31
stock: LCSC 39 759 pcs, JLCPCB assembly 54 977 pcs, Extended preferred (2026-10-31)

VDD 3.0–3.6 V, IREGIN ≤ 26 mA, θJA 32 °C/W, TA −40 … +85 °C (Table 3)
